product.label: Product
product.name: Field logistics (mobile)
product.description: Field representatives visit hospitals, work with surgeons, and manage the full part lifecycle—order, track, deliver, record surgical use, and return unused inventory—with preferences that persist across visits.

narrative.title: Problem
narrative.subtitle: Status lives in fragments
narrative.body: Reps, surgeons, and hospital ops each hold partial context. Orders, parts, deliveries, usage, and returns sit in different tools—so the next action is ambiguous under time pressure.

narrative.title: Solution
narrative.subtitle: One thumb path through the visit
narrative.body: A rep-primary mobile flow from arrive → preferences → order → track → deliver → use → return → request → close loop, with wireframes visible at every gallery beat.

claims.statement: Unify order, part, delivery, use, and return status so reps act in the hospital without calling ops
Surface surgeon preferences before reorder to reduce wrong-part risk and visit rework

resources.objective_notes: Design a single mobile path for field reps coordinating robotic surgery parts inside hospitals—from visit start through auditable close.
resources.method_notes: PM alignment on 10-beat IA, Sally hi-fi iPhone renders, lifecycle state model, and portfolio gallery wired to the case-study generator (HP field-service pattern).
resources.role_context: UX lead: problem framing with John, beat map and hi-fi spec with Sally, copy with Paige, package and publish with Winston/build.
constraints: Rep visits are time-boxed; status must be glanceable
Part serial/lot tracking is distinct from order rollup
Client outcome metrics are private—portfolio uses directional labels only
Event-registration / delegate flows are out of scope
insights: Preferences before order prevents wrong-kit rework on repeat visits.
Part-level status must not collapse into PO rollup alone.
Delivery splits shipment vs part-at-hospital (OR shelf) states.
Returns and new-part requests belong in the same app as orders.
quotes: I need to know if this serial is in the building—not just that the order shipped.
Surgeon prefs should show up before I build the cart again.
recommendations: Keep rep-primary IA; surface surgeon context without a second login.
Separate order track and part track beats in the gallery narrative.
Record surgical use with case ID for audit-friendly lifecycle.
Close each visit with open orders, returns due, and preference deltas visible.
